- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply +1–2% bias to first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment history with repeated 0.00 values, model tends to ignore trend; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract inertia.
